question: Which HARD program classes (multi-threaded contention, complex signals, mmap-heavy, epoll/io_uring) pass hermit run --strict --verify at L2 on the ptrace backend, and which expose frontier bugs?

host.note: --no-virtualize-cpuid required on this host (no usable CPUID faulting); orthogonal to scheduling/clock

frontier_bug_found.summary: delivery/consumption of a queued real-time signal (sigqueue/rt_sigqueueinfo) crashes the ptrace backend with 'wait after seccomp resume failed ... EINVAL' in ALL modes (--strict --verify, --strict, plain relaxed run).
frontier_bug_found.note: contradicts the read that #812 determinized rt_sigqueueinfo at ptrace L2; #812 likely covered send/return, not live same-thread delivery.

result: PASS: 3 hard guests (mmap-heavy, blocking multi-threaded producer/consumer, io_uring fallback) added to the hermit corpus, each a C guest + .rs harness pair with a default multi-run determinism test and an #[ignore]'d L2 --strict --verify test. All three reach L2 on the ptrace backend. One frontier signals bug localized and filed (see frontier_bug_found).
